_readme: External-verified enrichment layer for RSI v3/v6. Matched to graph project by case-insensitive substring on 'match'. v6 overrides: verified_enrichment_v6.json (profile, gates G1-G6, criteria K1-K14). reuse_scope also: single_trade, interior_fitout, platform_volume, unknown.

entries.donors_note: 25+ demolition/renovation projects & surplus stocks; incl. 21 hollow-core slabs from Regjeringskvartalet, ~70% steel, 1500 m² ceiling, ~2200 m² carpet, 20000 bricks.
entries.design_note: Bricks in lime mortar (removable), demountable extension units; but much in-situ integration. Independence moderate, exchangeability good.

entries.donors_note: Steel skeleton from Basel; stair/windows/granite from a Zürich office; further regional demolitions. >2700 components assessed; <100 km.
entries.reuse_share_note: >half of material second-used; 41% circular by volume, ~38% by weight.
entries.design_note: Layered, decoupled construction; visible/accessible structure designed to be taken apart (Brand layers; high exchangeability).

entries.reuse_share_note: ~90% of facade cladding reused; all windows/doors reused; foundation 42% RC-concrete. Facade-scoped.
entries.design_note: Glue-free single-material timber shell (beech dowels), type-separable, fully dismountable without quality loss — textbook Durmisevic exchangeability.

entries.co2_reduktion_note: 26% embodied-carbon cut vs concrete (21% timber + 5% reuse); Lendager LCA cites 30-50%. Reuse partial (salvaged aluminium facade, reused windows, turbine-blade shading).
entries.design_note: Mass-timber columns + CLT slabs (demountable), concrete only in cores; dual biogenic/circular ecosystems.

entries.canonical: Résilience – La Ferme des Possibles, Stains
entries.donors_note: Diffuse sources: Bellastock, Métabolisme Urbain, Réavie, leboncoin, Mairie de Paris + contractor salvage.
entries.reuse_share_note: 72.24 t reuse = 12.67% of total mass (fit-out + facade elements).
entries.design_note: Dry-assembly timber frame (glulam + CLT), straw+clay infill; largely biosourced with discrete reuse.

entries.reuse_share_note: 97% of the NEW external-core structural steel is reclaimed (steel-scoped, not whole building). 43% from 1 Broadgate + 57% via stockholder Cleveland Steel.
entries.design_note: Bolted external steel core; existing floorplates retained uninterrupted (layer independence).

entries.donors_note: Fire doors from Schulhaus Lavater (1:1), steel beams from a deconstruction, supermarket-trolley-depot pergola, lavabos/WCs from former flats, city second-hand furniture; 'Bauteiljagd'.
entries.design_note: Steel cut/re-plated/re-coated & bolted for reinstallation; components chosen for reversibility.

entries.donors_note: 100% BORROWED from many suppliers, producers and Eindhoven residents; returned unharmed after 9 days. Multi-source but temporary/borrowed (product-as-service), not owned.
entries.design_note: Zero-damage design: no screws/glue/drills/saws — steel straps & tension belts only. Maximal Durmisevic independence+exchangeability. The DfD reference case — but its scalability is limited by the temporary/borrowed model.

entries.donors_note: Steel structure from one textile 'paternoster' machine; facade from Twente cable reels; interior from local waste. Pioneered the 'Harvest Map' (Oogstkaart) sourcing method.
entries.reuse_share_note: ~60% of primary elements reused; steel structure 90% salvaged.
entries.design_note: Bolted salvaged-steel frame; design driven by harvested stock ('form follows availability'). Method (harvest map) is the transferable innovation.

entries.donors_note: Single-source closed loop: the existing 1967 factory itself is the material bank. TT-slabs cut & tilted into staircases, bricks into paving, doors recast into tabletops.
entries.reuse_share_note: DTU analysis: ~95% of original material reused/recycled; waste -90%.
entries.design_note: Radical in-situ structural reuse ('the building reuses itself'); bolted brackets/threaded rods/chemical anchors for new assemblies. High reuse execution; future-demountability moderate.

entries.reuse_share_note: CORRECTION: the widely cited '90%' is biosourced+reuse COMBINED (timber+straw), NOT 90% reuse. Actual reuse is discrete elements (reused windows, pavers, tiles, granite) — a minority of mass; 15% is a conservative estimate pending a published reuse-only figure.
entries.design_note: Dry-assembly ('filière sèche') prefabricated timber frame + straw cassettes — high adaptability/separability; reuse itself is modest.

entries.donors_note: Facade sourced from several regional demolitions <160 km: cut 1x1 m brick modules from the old Carlsberg Brewery + Aarhus schools; waste timber from Copenhagen Metro crates; repurposed factory bridge.
entries.reuse_share_note: Facade composed of 39% demolition-sourced material (roof 20%, wooden deck 5%). Building-level upcycle share ~29%; each reused brick saves ~500 g CO2 (~70% at brick level).
entries.design_note: Bricks are cement-mortar (not separable per brick) — sawn into 1x1 m panels tied to precast/timber. Upcycling into new composite panels rather than reversible DfD; separability low at component level.

entries.donors_note: World's first commercially scaled circular housing (20 row houses). 75% of windows from public housing in North Jutland; ~850-1400 t recycled-aggregate concrete from Copenhagen Metro waste; upcycled Dinesen wood offcuts for floors/walls/facades.
entries.reuse_share_note: ~2/3 of materials 'upcycled or reused' COMBINED — but a large part is recycled-aggregate concrete (recycling, not element reuse). Element reuse (75% windows + wood) is a subset; 40% is a conservative reuse-weighted estimate.
entries.design_note: DfD principles claimed, but recycled-aggregate concrete is cast in situ (not demountable); reused windows/wood are separable. Mixed: recycling-heavy, moderate exchangeability.

entries.donors_note: Smoked-glass facade panels harvested from the adjacent Knoop barracks (structure dimensioned to them); clinker pavers from an old Tiel quay; reused wood + furniture. Leased lift/light/furniture (product-as-service).
entries.design_note: Reference-grade demountable kit-of-parts: galvanized bolted steel frame, dry-assembled, even prefab-concrete-block foundations removable; parts independently reusable/recyclable. Paired with a closed 15-yr+1-day circular business case (leasing + buyback guarantee, ROI in 2-3 yrs) — the business-model exemplar.

entries.donors_note: First fully-circular NL building; broad urban-mining aggregation <100 km: monastery hardwood floor, window frames from a Philips office/Haarlem/Arnhem, 16 000 employee jeans + 2 500 kg workwear -> insulation/acoustic panels, fire-hose reels/cable ducts/pavers via urban miner New Horizon, bar from a football club, bench frames from canal bicycles.
entries.reuse_share_note: Many discrete reused components across trades (multi-source aggregator); no single whole-building reuse-% published.
entries.design_note: Bolted/clicked, glue-free assembly; larch skeleton left oversized so beams can be re-cut to standard planks; lifts/lighting leased; full digital twin / material register. High independence + exchangeability.

entries.canonical: Grande Halle de Colombelles (Encore Heureux / Le WIP)
entries.donors_note: Regional demolition sites (CU Caen la mer): 49 radiators, 10 oak doors (incl. fire door), sanitary, 190 m² tiles, 430 m² mineral wool, 21 wooden purlins. 21 windows identified but stolen before reuse.
entries.reuse_share_note: Concrete structure retained; reuse is interior fit-out. Reuse cost = 2% of the operation; discrete-element share of mass is small (~8% estimate).
entries.co2_einsparung_note: 11.4 t (Construction21) to 25.1 t CO2eq (Circle Economy) avoided; ~19-30 t waste diverted; 580 m³ CO2 saved.
entries.design_note: Structure kept, reversible fit-out. The real innovation is PROCUREMENT, not DfD: first building with a dedicated reuse work-package ('Lot 01', held by association Le WIP) + a variant/gap tender spec ('CCTP à trous') — a highly replicable contractual mechanism.

entries.donors_note: Single donor: a 7-storey 1982 Tampere office (deconstructed 2023 by Umacon/Skanska). 25 hollow-core slabs reclaimed, factory-refurbished at Consolis Parma, reused as floors above an air-raid shelter in the new A-Kruunu block.
entries.reuse_share_note: Mini-pilot: only 25 load-bearing slabs reused (small share of the new building) — a structural-reuse DEMONSTRATION, not a high whole-building quota.
entries.co2_reduktion_note: ReCreate reports up to 75% CO2 reduction at ELEMENT level for reused precast; no whole-building figure for this mini-pilot.
entries.design_note: Donor precast was NOT designed for disassembly (the core research challenge); proves salvage + factory QC + product approval of load-bearing precast. New frame is fully precast -> future reuse potential. Full-value-chain consortium (uni, demolisher, precast factory, engineer, architect, contractor, city).

entries.canonical: Kamikatsu Zero Waste Center 'WHY' (Hiroshi Nakamura & NAP)
entries.donors_note: Community-participation sourcing: ~700 windows/fixtures donated by residents of a town of <1 500; plus company-donated bricks/tiles/wood/fabric, deserted houses, a former government building, a closed junior-high, and shiitake-factory harvest containers.
entries.reuse_share_note: Predominantly built from salvaged materials; signature patchwork double-glazing facade from ~700 donated windows. No single reuse-% published.
entries.design_note: Unprocessed cedar logs sawn + bolted into trusses that can be disassembled/reused; separable structure. Patchwork window facade is bespoke (each unit measured/positioned by software) rather than a systematic product — high craft, moderate replicability.

entries.donors_note: Former Kindl brewery warehouse retrofit + GLT/CLT rooftep extension. Steel purlins from the hall's own roof reused as load-bearing stair stringers; removed steel trusses planned for the greenhouse roof; second-hand windows + fire doors.
entries.design_note: New components joined with reversible connectors and planned in layers (Brand); short-life technical elements accessible/exchangeable without destruction; burn-down timber (F90 without encapsulation for material purity); material passports. German cooperative model (TRNSFRM eG) + CH->DE knowledge transfer via baubüro in situ + KfW/IBB funding — highly relevant to the DE funding context.

entries.canonical: Impact Hub Berlin / CRCLR interior fit-out (LXSY)
entries.donors_note: 500 m² co-working fit-out; ~70% reused/recycled/upcycled materials (steel beams, windows, fire doors). Built largely DIY by a collective of few craftsmen + many laypersons after COVID left no contractors.
entries.design_note: Interior planned along circular lines: recyclable materials + elements designed for easy disassembly/repurposing, documented with product/material passports. Fit-out-scoped; strong exchangeability, DIY-built.

entries.donors_note: 3 750 reclaimed oak window frames salvaged from renovation/demolition sites across ALL EU member states, sanded/restored/varnished and set in stainless-steel frames — a cross-border aggregation forming the double-facade outer skin ('United in Diversity').
entries.reuse_share_note: Reuse is the decorative/acoustic outer facade skin only; the rest of the 53 815 m² superstructure is new. Whole-building reuse mass share is small.
entries.co2_reduktion_note: Facade structure uses ~30% less steel than a classic facade; no whole-building reuse LCA published.
entries.design_note: Landmark LARGE-SCALE facade-reuse aggregation with high political/symbolic legitimation value, but the windows are a fixed decorative skin (bespoke, not a systemic DfD strategy). Its lever is legitimation + cross-border sourcing, not transformation capacity.
